It's pretty clear that by taking these moves, Microsoft is attempting to add value to their entire Windows 10 ecosystem. It is interesting that MS is making the console gaming more PC-like while Valve's big push with Steam Machines were to make PC gaming more console like. Valve's Steam Machines are going to become even more irrelevant in that it will ALWAYS be cheaper to purchase a subsidized XBox than it will be to buy a Steam Machine. Plus, providing the "play anywhere" feature will make buying games from Microsoft an attractive proposition if you do both PC and console gaming.
